Thought: I need to determine the number of resonances in the proton (1H) and carbon (13C) NMR spectra of p-xylene (1,4-dimethylbenzene). To do this, I'll analyze the structure and identify the chemically equivalent protons and carbons.

p-xylene (1,4-dimethylbenzene) has the following structure:
- A benzene ring with methyl groups at positions 1 and 4 (para to each other)
- The structure has symmetry which will affect the number of distinct signals

For proton (1H) NMR:
- The protons in the two methyl groups are equivalent due to symmetry (one signal)
- The aromatic protons at positions 2, 3, 5, and 6 are all equivalent due to symmetry (one signal)
- So there are 2 distinct proton environments, giving 2 signals in the 1H NMR

For carbon (13C) NMR (decoupled):
- The two methyl carbons are equivalent (one signal)
- The two carbons where the methyl groups are attached (C1 and C4) are equivalent (one signal)
- The remaining four aromatic carbons (C2, C3, C5, C6) are all equivalent due to symmetry (one signal)
- So there are 3 distinct carbon environments, giving 3 signals in the 13C NMR

Therefore, p-xylene will show 2 signals in the proton NMR and 3 signals in the carbon NMR.
Final Answer: The p-xylene molecule will have 2 signals in the proton (1H) NMR spectrum and 3 signals in the carbon (13C) NMR spectrum. Looking at the options, this corresponds to option B: 2H, 3C.
